sourceNote.title: Invoice PDF export
sourceNote.html:
Invoice PDF export

Testing the Export PDF action on the invoice detail page of a demo accounting app.

  • Invoice states: draft, sent, paid, cancelled. Only sent and paid invoices can be exported; draft and cancelled show the button disabled with a tooltip.

  • The PDF contains company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate (0%, 9%, 21%) and totals.

  • Invoices with more than 25 line items continue on a second page with the header repeated.

  • File name is invoice-<number>.pdf.

  • Observed: an invoice with a customer name containing "Müller & Söhne" exported fine, but the ampersand looked escaped in the file name preview.

  • Observed: export of a 60-line invoice took about 8 seconds with no progress indicator.

bodyHtml:
Decision table overview: Export PDF on invoice detail page

Conditions:

  • C1: Invoice state (draft, sent, paid, cancelled)

  • C2: Number of line items (25 or fewer, more than 25)

  • C3: VAT rates on the line items (0%, 9%, 21%)

  • C4: Customer name contains special characters (for example "Müller & Söhne")

Actions:

  • A1: Export PDF button is enabled and the export runs

  • A2: Export PDF button is disabled and a tooltip is shown

  • A3: PDF contains company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate and totals

  • A4: Line items continue on a second page with the header repeated

  • A5: File name is invoice-<number>.pdf

Rules:

  • R1: State = sent → A1, A3, A5

  • R2: State = paid → A1, A3, A5

  • R3: State = draft → A2

  • R4: State = cancelled → A2

  • R5: State = sent or paid, 25 or fewer line items → A1, A3, A5, single page (no A4)

  • R6: State = sent or paid, more than 25 line items → A1, A3, A4, A5

  • R7: State = sent or paid, VAT rates 0%, 9% and 21% present → A3 with VAT shown separately per rate

  • R8: State = sent or paid, customer name with special characters → A1, A3, A5

Gap: The note does not say how 0% VAT lines look in the PDF, how many pages an invoice with more than 50 line items should have, or what the file name preview should show. Where these cases touch on those points, they check only what the note states.

Scenario: Export availability by invoice state

Test case: Export PDF is enabled for a sent invoice (R1)

Purpose: Verify that a sent invoice can be exported to PDF.

Preconditions: The demo accounting app is open and an invoice in the sent state exists.

Test data: One invoice in the sent state with at least one line item.

  • Open the invoice detail page of the sent invoice.

  • Check the state of the Export PDF button.

  • Click Export PDF.

  • Open the downloaded PDF.

Expected result: The Export PDF button is enabled. A PDF is produced that contains the company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate and totals.

Coverage notes: Rule R1, state condition C1 = sent. Positive case.

Test case: Export PDF is enabled for a paid invoice (R2)

Purpose: Verify that a paid invoice can be exported to PDF.

Preconditions: The demo accounting app is open and an invoice in the paid state exists.

Test data: One invoice in the paid state with at least one line item.

  • Open the invoice detail page of the paid invoice.

  • Check the state of the Export PDF button.

  • Click Export PDF.

  • Open the downloaded PDF.

Expected result: The Export PDF button is enabled. A PDF is produced that contains the company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate and totals.

Coverage notes: Rule R2, state condition C1 = paid. Positive case.

Test case: Export PDF is disabled with a tooltip for a draft invoice (R3)

Purpose: Verify that a draft invoice cannot be exported and the user is told why.

Preconditions: The demo accounting app is open and an invoice in the draft state exists.

Test data: One invoice in the draft state.

  • Open the invoice detail page of the draft invoice.

  • Check the state of the Export PDF button.

  • Hover over the Export PDF button.

  • Try to click Export PDF.

Expected result: The Export PDF button is disabled and a tooltip is shown on hover. No PDF is produced.

Coverage notes: Rule R3, negative case. The note does not give the tooltip text, so only check that a tooltip appears.

Test case: Export PDF is disabled with a tooltip for a cancelled invoice (R4)

Purpose: Verify that a cancelled invoice cannot be exported and the user is told why.

Preconditions: The demo accounting app is open and an invoice in the cancelled state exists.

Test data: One invoice in the cancelled state.

  • Open the invoice detail page of the cancelled invoice.

  • Check the state of the Export PDF button.

  • Hover over the Export PDF button.

  • Try to click Export PDF.

Expected result: The Export PDF button is disabled and a tooltip is shown on hover. No PDF is produced.

Coverage notes: Rule R4, negative case. Together with R1 to R3, this covers all four invoice states.

Scenario: PDF content and pagination

Test case: 25 line items fit on a single page (R5, boundary)

Purpose: Verify that an invoice with exactly 25 line items, the highest count before the second-page rule applies, does not continue on a second page.

Preconditions: An exportable (sent or paid) invoice with exactly 25 line items exists.

Test data: A sent or paid invoice with 25 line items.

  • Open the invoice detail page and click Export PDF.

  • Open the PDF and count the line items and pages.

Expected result: All 25 line items are in the PDF and the line items do not continue on a second page.

Coverage notes: Rule R5, boundary on C2. The note says only that invoices with "more than 25" line items go to a second page, so the single-page result for 25 items is inferred from that rule.

Test case: 26 line items continue on a second page with the header repeated (R6, boundary)

Purpose: Verify that the first count above 25 line items moves to a second page and repeats the header there.

Preconditions: An exportable (sent or paid) invoice with exactly 26 line items exists.

Test data: A sent or paid invoice with 26 line items.

  • Open the invoice detail page and click Export PDF.

  • Open the PDF and go to the second page.

  • Compare the header on page 2 with the header on page 1.

  • Check that all 26 line items appear across both pages, with none missing or repeated.

Expected result: The line items continue on a second page, and the header is repeated on that page.

Coverage notes: Rule R6, boundary on C2 (25/26).

Test case: A 60-line invoice exports across pages with the header repeated (R6)

Purpose: Verify that a large invoice exports completely and paginates with repeated headers, and record how long the export takes.

Preconditions: An exportable (sent or paid) invoice with 60 line items exists.

Test data: A sent or paid invoice with 60 line items.

  • Open the invoice detail page and click Export PDF.

  • Time how long the export takes and note whether any progress indicator appears.

  • Open the PDF and check that the header is repeated on each continuation page.

  • Check that all 60 line items and the totals are present.

Expected result: The PDF contains all 60 line items. The line items continue past the first page with the header repeated, and the totals are present.

Coverage notes: Rule R6 with a large line-item count. Evidence from the note: exporting a 60-line invoice took about 8 seconds and showed no progress indicator. Record the time you measure for comparison. The note does not state an expected export time.

Test case: VAT is shown separately for each rate, with correct totals (R7)

Purpose: Verify that the PDF shows VAT separately for 0%, 9% and 21% and that the totals match.

Preconditions: An exportable (sent or paid) invoice exists with line items at 0%, 9% and 21% VAT.

Test data: A sent or paid invoice with at least one line item at each VAT rate: 0%, 9% and 21%.

  • Open the invoice detail page and click Export PDF.

  • In the PDF, find the VAT amount for each of the 0%, 9% and 21% rates.

  • Compare the VAT amounts and totals in the PDF with the invoice detail page.

  • Check that the company logo, invoice number, dates and line items are present.

Expected result: The PDF shows the VAT for each rate (0%, 9%, 21%) and totals that match the invoice. The logo, invoice number, dates and line items are all present.

Coverage notes: Rule R7, condition C3, covering all three rates. To test each rate on its own, repeat the case with an invoice that uses a single rate.

Scenario: Export file naming

Test case: The file name follows invoice-<number>.pdf (A5)

Purpose: Verify that the exported file is named after the invoice number.

Preconditions: An exportable (sent or paid) invoice exists.

Test data: A sent or paid invoice. Write down its invoice number from the detail page.

  • Open the invoice detail page and write down the invoice number.

  • Click Export PDF.

  • Check the name of the downloaded file.

Expected result: The file is named invoice-<number>.pdf, where <number> is the invoice number.

Coverage notes: Action A5. Run this case with both a sent and a paid invoice.

Test case: Customer name with special characters: "Müller & Söhne" (R8)

Purpose: Verify that an invoice whose customer name contains umlauts and an ampersand exports correctly, and check the file name preview.

Preconditions: An exportable (sent or paid) invoice exists for the customer "Müller & Söhne".

Test data: Customer name "Müller & Söhne" on a sent or paid invoice.

  • Open the invoice detail page and click Export PDF.

  • Look at the file name preview and note how the ampersand is shown.

  • Check the name of the downloaded file.

  • Open the PDF and check the content.

Expected result: The export succeeds. The file is named invoice-<number>.pdf, and the PDF contains the expected invoice content.

Coverage notes: Rule R8, condition C4 (special characters). Evidence from the note: this invoice exported fine, but the ampersand looked escaped in the file name preview. Record exactly what the preview shows. The note does not say why the customer name affects the preview when the file name rule uses only the invoice number.
